messages:
Dana Liu: Quick Q  I checked into a hotel for a 3-day customer visit. My folio has a bunch of incidental charges: valet $48, minibar $12, Wi-Fi $15/day, and a mandatory resort fee $25. Which of these are reimbursable?
people-ops-bot: Travel policy extract -> reimbursable: business-related charges (parking/valet when used for client travel), reasonable internet if required for work, laundry for trips >3 days with approval. Non-reimbursable: minibar, in-room movies, personal expenses, mandatory resort fees unless pre-approved. See travel guide: https://intranet/redwood/te/hotel-incidental (auto-note)
Marcus Green: We often have to pay resort fees in some cities. Is there a cap or do we need pre-approval to claim them?
Talia Nguyen: Short policy practicals from travel ops:
- Valet/parking: reimbursable when used for work meetings; keep receipt. If parking is >$40/day, include justification (airport vs downtown event).
- Wi-Fi: reimbursable if you need it for meetings or remote work; otherwise personal wifi is non-reimbursable. Attach a short note in Concur: "required for client demo".
- Minibar: non-reimbursable unless it's a documented business meal (e.g., bought snacks for client) with names and receipts.
- Resort fees: generally non-reimbursable unless unavoidable and approved ahead of travel. If hotel bundles core amenities needed for work, get manager pre-approval and add note + hotel policy screenshot.
Ethan Brooks: What about tips included on folio vs cash tips? Also currency conversion when charging on personal card abroad?
Talia Nguyen: For tips: include them on the folio (card tips) or add a separate receipt for cash tips. We reimburse reasonable tipping for taxis/valet/porters; attach receipts where possible. For foreign transactions: submit the original foreign currency receipt and your card statement showing conversion. Concur will accept the foreign amount; finance will apply the bank conversion rate.
Dana Liu: If the hotel charges minibar by room but I didn't consume it, how do I dispute it if I only have the folio?
Marcus Green: Call front desk to get an itemized folio or incident report. Hotels can remove erroneous charges; save emails. Upload the corrected folio to Concur with a short note.
Talia Nguyen: Filing tips:
```
Expense type: Hotel Incidental
Policy code: TRV-HOTEL-INC-2026
Required attachments: itemized folio, receipts for parking/Wi-Fi/tips, manager pre-approval (if resort fee or > $40 valet)
Notes: explain business purpose for any atypical line items
```
Dana Liu: Great, I'll request an itemized folio and unbundle the charges. Thanks! :thumbsup:
Ethan Brooks: One last: if the corporate card pays the folio, do we still need receipts?
Talia Nguyen: If corporate card covers it, keep receipts for audit trail; mark as paid by corporate card. For small incidental charges (< $10) we sometimes accept a screenshot but try to keep originals.
Dana Liu: Filing now. Appreciate the help.
